## Mixed models for the repeated visits {.unnumbered}

The cleaned data are in long format, with up to five rows per patient. Rows from the same patient are not independent, and chapter 3 showed it with the correlation between visits. A plain regression would treat them as independent. Ignoring the correlation gives the wrong standard errors, often too small for comparisons between arms.

A mixed model fixes this. It gives each patient their own starting level and, if needed, their own slope. It also uses every visit a patient attended, so it copes with the dropout we built in. That is the next chapter.
